subject: Request: TTL/Erasure artifacts and retention mapping for SOC2 audit - ClearHarbor
messages:
From: Aisha Rana <aisha@clearharbor.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: audits@clearharbor.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2: sample exports + TTL proof request

Hi Kimberly,

As part of our upcoming SOC 2 Type II audit, our auditors have requested a small set of artifacts to validate tenant-level TTL and deletion controls for data stored with Redwood Inference. Specifically they asked for:

- An example tenant export showing item-level timestamps (created_at, last_accessed, ttl_expiry) and retention metadata
- The corresponding erasure run log showing the deletion job that handled the tenant once TTL was reached (including job id, start/end timestamps, and status)
- A mapping document that ties retention policy names to where data is stored (region, storage class) and the control owner

Can you confirm if you can provide redacted examples (PII removed) and indicate whether the erasure log includes cryptographic proof (hashes) or only operational status? We need these by 2026-08-31 to hit audit deadlines.

Thanks,
Aisha Rana
Head of Security Operations
ClearHarbor

----- Original Message Follow-up -----

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Rana <aisha@clearharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2: sample exports + TTL proof request

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide redacted exports and the erasure run log. A couple quick clarifications so we give the auditors exactly what they need:

1) For the "cryptographic proof" item — our deletion pipeline emits content hashes for object stores and a job-level checksum for the run output. We don't currently notarize those hashes with an external timestamping authority; do your auditors require that level?

2) Which tenant(s) should we sample? We can provide one production tenant (anonymized) and one sandbox tenant to show differences in storage class/retention.

3) Preferred format for the mapping doc? We can produce an Excel that maps policy name -> retention TTL -> storage backend -> region -> control owner.

I'll start assembling redacted artifacts and will loop in Priyom and Vivek for the erasure logs and the export extract.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance (for Redwood Inference)

----- Reply (internal) -----
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2: sample exports + TTL proof request

Kimberly —

I pulled the extractor and erasure pipeline artifacts:
- Export: we can generate a CSV that includes created_at, last_written_at, ttl_expiry, retention_policy_id, storage_bucket, region (redacted tenant IDs). We'll scrub all PII per our standard redaction script.
- Erasure run log: the deletion job logs job_id, start_ts, end_ts, items_deleted_count, status, and per-object checksum (SHA256) for objects removed from S3/Blob. The job-level report includes a SHA256 of the concatenated object checksums (this is our internal checksum not externally timestamped).
- Mapping doc: I'll assemble retention_mapping_clearharbor_v20260829.xlsx covering policy names used by ClearHarbor accounts.

I recommend including both a production-sample and sandbox-sample so auditors see both lifecycle classes.

I'll attach the working files to this thread for review and redaction confirmation.

- Priyom
Senior Compliance Engineer

----- Internal Note (Vivek) -----
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2: sample exports + TTL proof request

Attached the sample export and run log (redacted placeholders in the sample). A few operational caveats to call out for auditors:

- TTL is enforced by the erasure scheduler which triggers region-specific workers; there can be a 0-30 minute scheduling drift depending on backlog. Our SLO is 1 hour for tenant-level deletion once TTL crosses.
- For cross-region replication we delete primary and then issue tombstones to replicas; replication lag can cause replica deletion to happen slightly later (we capture that in the run log).
- If auditors need proof of deletion from the cloud provider (e.g., S3 object delete markers and versioning records), we can pull the provider-side manifests under an evidence request but that requires our infra team to open a job with cloud provider compliance channels (adds ~48h).

Attaching: clearharbor_export_sample_2026-06.csv, erasure_runlog-tenant-3491.txt

-Vivek
Head of Site Reliability
